content:
maddy: Heads-up — saw a spike of `validator.soft_coercion` in the telemetry for fncall responses this morning. Lots of requests showing "coerced array -> string" and then routing to the degen route. Anyone know why we're quietly coercing instead of rejecting?

leo: Hmm. Which model/route? and is this user-facing or internal tool calls?

maddy: Route is `assistant.tools.v2` on prod-us-east, model variant `redwood-v1-std`. It's from customer sandbox traffic hitting a new schema that returns `items: ["a"]` vs expected `items: {name:string}`. We coerce silently to keep downstream adapters from exploding.

sam: We intentionally soft-coerce in the validator lib for backwards compat, but agree we haven't surfaced it well. Dashboard only shows reject counts, not soft coercions.

console-bot: Alert: validator.soft_coercion rate increased 6x over last 2h on route assistant.tools.v2 (sampled trace ids attached).

dina: Can you paste an example payload?

maddy: Sure — example snippet: ```json
{"tool_response": {"items": ["ok"]}}
// validator interpreted as {"items": {"name": "ok"}} and coerced
```

amy: Oof. That exact coercion can hide real schema drift. From a UX/ops perspective we should: 1) expose coercions in the console (per-route small table), 2) add a sampling pipeline that grabs raw payloads when coercion happens, 3) tag telemetry with "coercion_reason" so alerts can be meaningful.

leo: +1 on tagging. Also we need to think about billing/quota — if we treat coerced calls as successful, customers get billed but may have incorrect behavior. Should coerced = billed but mark in billing export?

sam: Proposal: keep billing as-is (success = bill), but add a new billing flag `validation_coercion` exported once daily. That way finance can reconcile if needed.

dina: For rollouts: when enabling stricter validate gate, we need a canary that surfaces coercion counts and sample payloads in the rollout UI. Otherwise teams flip strict on and stuff breaks silently.

maddy: Agreed. Also want an ops alarm when coercion rate > x% of total invokes for 15m, with automatic creation of a sampling ticket (linked to console trace).

leo: Implementation notes: validator currently does coercion in `validate_and_normalize()` path. We can emit an event `validation.coercion` with payload hash and reason. Need to ensure payloads are sampled (<1%) to avoid PII leaks.

amy: We should also add a small UX affordance: in the route details view show a mini timeline: Rejects / Coercions / Soft-fallbacks. Toggle to include sample (requires opt-in).

sam: Risk: exposing samples could hit compliance for some customers. Add a redaction pipeline and opt-in per-project for raw samples. Default to structured metadata only.

dina: Who owns the dashboard change + telemetry schema? I can take dashboard card. @leo can you own the event emission and schema? @sam can you update validator lib to tag and sample?

leo: I can own emission/schema. I'll draft an event contract: fields `route`, `model_variant`, `coercion_type`, `coercion_reason`, `trace_id`, `sampled_payload_id` (optional).

sam: I'll add tagging in validator and a sampling hook that writes to redacted-samples S3 when opted-in. Will also add a metric `validation.coercion.count` with dimensions.

amy: I'll wire the console card and add a toggle for "Show sampled payloads" with clear privacy copy.

maddy: Thanks. Can we aim for a small canary next week? If we surface this, we can avoid a bunch of surprise breakages during stricter validate rollout.

leo: timeline: event contract PR by EOD Thu, sampling impl by next Tue, dashboard card prototype Wed.

sam: note: we should also decide whether coercions count toward graceful-fallback SLOs. Filing an RFC follow-up.

dina: Sounds good. Creating a quick ticket: https://tickets.redwoodinc/ENG-9123 with owners.

maddy: perfect — leaving here. Ping owners in #eng-platform when PRs are up. :thumbsup:
